root.claim: A deterministic fixed-tape Turing machine multiplies $n$-bit integers exactly in $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$ time with $\kappa=2^{-182}$.
root.method: build two tape procedures that save a power of the width, use them inside the Harvey and van der Hoeven Gaussian-resampling multiplication with polynomial transforms and retained permutations, then choose parameters, prove exactness and sum the costs

motivation.text: Scanning the data at each of $\log n$ transform levels already costs $n\log n$, so beating it needs savings in both movement and arithmetic.

quote.quote: We therefore need savings in both movement and arithmetic.

root.salient: The exponent $\kappa=2^{-182}$ is astronomically small, yet strictly positive: the saving is a power of $\log n$ for all input lengths, and it disproves the $n\log n$ conjecture in this model.
